data.name: Elysia
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word ‘Elysium’, meaning ‘heavenly’ or ‘divine’. In Greek mythology, Elysium was the paradise where the heroic and virtuous dead went after death. In Christian symbolism, Elysia represents a heavenly paradise, a place of peace, beauty, and eternal life.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of the eternal paradise and peace found in Christianity.

in_hebrew.name: אליסיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אליסיה היא שם נשים המקורב לאלוהי ואהוב, שהגיע משמעות שמותי של אלישע, נביא ישראלי, שבעצת אלוהים, נטע חיים (1 מלכים 19:16).

in_greek.name: Ελυσιά
in_greek.long_meaning: Ελυσιά είναι γυναικείο όνομα που προέρχεται από το όνομα Ελισσαι, το οποίο είναι σύνθετο από τους όρους Ελ και σία. Η Ελισσαι είναι μια από τις τρεις γυναίκες που απεκαταστάθηκαν από τον Ιησού από τον θάνατο (Ματθαίος 27:55-56).

in_latin.name: Elysia
in_latin.long_meaning: Elysia est nomen mulieris quod significat 'Deus exaltavit, amor aeternus'. Origine venit a nomine Elisae, quod compositum est ex verbis deus et aeternus. Elisae est una ex tribus mulieribus quae a Iesu a morte resurrectae sunt (Matthaeus 27:55-56).

in_english.name: Elysia
in_english.meaning: God exalted, love eternal, heavenly delight, blessed by God
in_english.long_meaning: Elysia is a feminine given name that means 'God exalted, love eternal, heavenly delight, blessed by God.' It originates from the name Elisae, which is a compound of the words God and eternal. Elisae is one of the three women resurrected by Jesus from the dead (Matthew 27:55-56). This name is associated with qualities such as devotion, love, and spiritual growth. In modern times, Elysia is used across various Christian cultures to commemorate the significance of divine love and redemption.
